title: Woman who died in cell had health issues
article: A fatality inquiry has heard that a northern Alberta woman who died in an RCMP holding cell got a prescription for 100 tablets of a strong narcotic painkiller less than 72 hours before her death.
Dr. Andries Botha testified that Colleen Marie Akazay, who died Feb. 18, 2006, had health issues ranging from chronic back aches to depression, as well as anxiety and stress disorders.
Botha said he warned Akazay on numerous occasions not to exceed the maximum dosage of Tylenol 4, which contains the narcotic codeine, and bromazepam.
But Botha also said on a few occasions he wrote her new prescriptions when she claimed she had either lost or been robbed of her medication.
RCMP Const. Helen Pappas told the inquiry last week that Akazay was alert and coherent when she was taken into custody.
But that contradicts the testimony of a cellmate, who told the inquiry that Akazay was having trouble staying awake, going to the bathroom and getting into bed.

Pappas's testimony was also at odds with the booking sheet filled out when Akazay was brought in to the cells. The sheet had marked ''falling'' for balance and ''incoherent'' in the section for speech, but Pappas said she was not the officer who wrote those observations.
The fatality inquiry has been adjourned and will resume next year. No date has been set.
Public inquiries are limited to establishing the cause, manner, time, place and circumstances of death, as well as the identity of the deceased.
The judge may make recommendations on the prevention of similar occurrences.
